precepts.text: Meditate on the book of the law day and night and observe to do all written in it, and thy way shall be prosperous and have good success.
precepts.point: If you are planted in the house of the Lord, that means you are applying these things that keep you grounded in this truth.

note.label: Psalm 92: Planted in the House of the Lord

precepts.why:
“Those that be planted in the house of the Lord shall flourish in the courts of our God.” Listen to the terminology: those that be planted take root, meaning you start to gain understanding because you are focused on the word and meditating on it. Joshua was told how: “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.”

Meditate on the book of the law day and night and observe to do all that is written in it, and your way shall be prosperous and have good success. That is how the righteous flourish like the palm tree and grow like a cedar in Lebanon.

If you are planted in the house of the Lord, that means you are applying these things that keep you grounded in this truth. The meditating and the doing are the roots.

precepts.text: All unrighteousness is sin, and there is a sin not unto death.
precepts.point: There is no sin in the Most High. Our people may struggle saying you cannot keep all the laws, but the Most High says His laws are not grievous and He did not give any man permission to sin.

note.label: Psalm 92: Planted in the House of the Lord

precepts.why:
The righteous bring forth fruit in old age “To shew that the Lord is upright: he is my rock, and there is no unrighteousness in him.” John tells what unrighteousness is: “All unrighteousness is sin: and there is a sin not unto death.”

All unrighteousness is sin, so there being no unrighteousness in the Most High means there is no sin in him. He is upright, and he is our rock. And there is a sin not unto death, so those planted in his house who stumble are not cut off; they still bring forth fruit and show that he is upright.

precepts.text: He hath commanded no man to do wickedly, neither hath He given any man license to sin.
precepts.point: There is no sin in the Most High. Our people may struggle saying you cannot keep all the laws, but the Most High says His laws are not grievous and He did not give any man permission to sin.

note.label: Psalm 92: Planted in the House of the Lord

precepts.why:
There is no unrighteousness in the Most High, and he gives none to us either. “He hath commanded no man to do wickedly, neither hath he given any man licence to sin.”

Our people may struggle, saying you cannot keep all the laws, but the Most High says his laws are not grievous, and he did not give any man permission to sin. He commanded no man to do wickedly.

So those planted in his house are to be fat and flourishing in righteousness even in old age, to show that the Lord is upright. If there is no unrighteousness in him and no licence to sin from him, then keeping his law is what shows he is our rock.
